title: Lost Account Resuscitation — Rapid Diagnostic & Playbook Draft
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a lightweight, repeatable diagnostic + resuscitation playbook intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs) to run within 72 hours after a renewal decline or sudden account exit. Goal: quickly convert ambiguity into a prioritized set of hypotheses, one short experiment to attempt recovery, and clear handoffs if the account is lost.

When to use this doc:
- Renewal declined in negotiation window with incomplete rationale from buyer.
- Sudden stop of usage/paused billing without clear support ticket history.
- Executive-level pushback (procurement/security) that threatens committed ARR.

Quick summary (one-line):
- What happened: [short sentence summarizing top-level signal and timestamp]
- Immediate ask: Run resuscitation experiment A within 7 days / escalate to AE + Solutions if experiment fails.

High-level triage ladder (first 72 hours):
1) Signal capture (owner: CSM, due: day 0)
   - Confirm renewal status, PO/contract stage, churn reason recorded in CRM.
   - Pull usage telemetry (token/requests, embeddings calls, endpoint errors) for last 30 and last 7 days.
   - Check support and SRE tickets for regressions that align with timeline.
2) Quick hypothesis sprint (owner: CSM + SE, due: day 1)
   - Form 2–4 root-cause hypotheses (see template below).
   - For each hypothesis, list 1 piece of evidence that would falsify it.
3) Rescue experiment selection (owner: CSM + AE, due: day 2)
   - Pick highest-likelihood, lowest-effort experiment (trial extension, targeted mitigation, PO reformat, exec introduction).
   - Commit to experiment parameters: duration, success metric, owner.
4) Execute and monitor (owner: experiment owner, due: days 2–7)
   - Run experiment, collect telemetry, and keep AE/PM updated daily.
5) Decision & next steps (owner: CSM, due: day 7)
   - Convert to win (renewal + commit) OR capture an entry-level postmortem and offboarding checklist if lost.

Root-cause hypothesis template (short):
- Hypothesis ID: H1
- Claim: e.g., "Model latency spike caused reduced usage and negative stakeholder sentiment."
- Why it explains departure: [one sentence]
- Key evidence to check: e.g., 95th-percentile latency logs for date range
- Quick falsifier: e.g., latency normal => deprioritize
- Recommended quick fix: e.g., change deployment to lower-latency variant + 2-week trial at no charge

Example hypotheses (illustrative):
- H1: Billing or contract terms miscommunication (billing hold or PO format). Evidence: contract emails and procurement requests.
- H2: Regression in model quality after a model swap leading to wrong outputs. Evidence: customer prompt set fails in eval subset.
- H3: Latency/cost spike on their site created internal pressure to pause. Evidence: platform telemetry and SRE incidents.
- H4: Strategic reprioritization (budget reallocation). Evidence: customer roadmap updates, public funding or hiring freeze signals.

Resuscitation experiments (pick one, low-friction first):
- Soft-extension: 30-day renewal extension with clear success metric (usage threshold or time-bound POC).
- Targeted technical mitigation: temporary model pinning or quantization rollback to restore quality/latency.
- Executive coffee: AE + CRO intro to buyer execs for re-evaluation and potential concession framing.
- Purchase workflow patch: provide a formatted PO template and a named billing contact to reduce procurement friction.
- Workspace restart: a dedicated SE session to rebuild prompt templates and demo regression fixes.

Mini renewal-tracker (single-row template explained):
Fields (as CSV-style columns): account, ARR_at_risk, renewal_date, decision_channel, stated_reason, primary_evidence, experiment_selected, owner, experiment_due, result, next_action
Example row (values):
"Acme Retail, $120k, 2026-01-20, procurement_hold, latency & cost, 95p latency increased 2.3x, pin model + 30d extension, Asha Nair, 2026-01-27, partial-success (usage restored 65%), schedule exec review"

Decision criteria for experiments (success/fail):
- Primary success: customer reactivates usage to >= 70% of baseline AND agrees to a renewal conversation.
- Secondary success: procurement shows progress (PO submitted) or technical blockers removed.
- Fail: no traction after experiment window OR new blocker surfaces requiring >30d remediation.

Postmortem mini-template (if account is lost):
- Executive summary (3 lines)
- Timeline of key events (date/time + event + owner)
- Root-cause hypotheses and evidence (keep top 3)
- Counterfactuals considered (what we would have tried earlier)
- Key lessons (3 bullets)
- Suggested playbook changes (3–5 actionable items, owner, ETA)
- Hand-off checklist for offboarding: data export, support expiry, knowledge transfer, CS churn survey

Example timeline (short):
- 2025-10-20 09:12 — Sales notified CSM of renewal delay (Owner: AE)
- 2025-10-23 14:05 — Usage dropped 78% after model swap (Owner: Platform)
- 2025-10-25 10:00 — Procurement asked for PO template and compliance certs (Owner: Buyer)
- 2025-10-28 16:00 — CSM ran initial diagnostics and scheduled SE runbook (Owner: CSM)

Counterfactual thinking (structured):
- Action we might have taken earlier: e.g., weekly telemetry digest to customer champions starting 90 days pre-renewal.
- Expected effect: earlier detection of signal; opportunity to correct model swap before broad impact.
- Cost/effort: low (automated digest), owner: product-ops.

Playbook change candidates (prioritized):
1) Pre-renewal observability digest (owner: product-ops, ETA: 6 weeks) — low cost, high signal coverage.
2) Procurement SOP card (owner: CS operations, ETA: 3 weeks) — template PO + compliance FAQ.
3) Fast-path model-pinning option (owner: serving-runtime + eng-product, ETA: 10 weeks) — reduce rollback time.

Internal comms snippets (for AE/CSM use):
- Short email to buyer: "We ran a focused check on [issue]. We’d like to offer a 30-day extension + a one-hour SE-led remediation session. If that helps, we can re-open the renewal conversation — Asha Nair, CSM."
- Exec intro note: "[AE], looping in our VP of Solutions, Priya, who can coordinate a short health check and propose a low-friction fix to unblock procurement. We value the partnership and want to make this right."

Measurement & learning log (track over time):
- Metric candidates: renewal conversion after rescue (binary), time from signal-to-action (hours), # of rescue experiments per quarter, rescue experiment success rate, average ARR recovered.
- Keep a short running log per account: date, experiment, result, learning (one sentence).

Notes and caveats:
- This document is intentionally pragmatic and minimal — the objective is to convert murky churn signals into a testable action within 72 hours.
- Not every lost account is recoverable; capture learnings and prioritize future prevention (product/ops changes) over chasing low-probability rescues.

Next steps (for this draft):
- Review with CS leadership and solutions engineering (due: next weekly CS leadership sync).
- Pilot on 3 at-risk accounts next quarter and capture results in the measurement log.

Appendix: quick checklist (tick-box style as text)
- [ ] CRM renewal status verified
- [ ] Top-3 hypotheses documented
- [ ] Rescue experiment chosen and owner assigned
- [ ] Daily telemetry checks scheduled during experiment
- [ ] Exec/escalation path documented
- [ ] Post-experiment decision recorded

Contact notes: Asha Nair — asha.nair@redwood-inference.com — CSM lead for pilot.

End of document.
